title: Delegation brief: standing authorization + effort-scaling rules in CLAUDE.md, replacing policy prose
description: Two changes to CLAUDE.md's tiering section. (1) STANDING AUTHORIZATION: this session's harness system prompt contains 'Do not call the Agent tool unless the user requested it' — grep found it in no user-editable file, so it is harness-injected. It directly countermands CLAUDE.md's delegate-first design, and the closer instruction wins, which reframes the measured inline-heavy behaviour as partial compliance rather than pure judgement failure. The line's own carve-out is 'unless the user requested it', so CLAUDE.md must state explicitly that delegation per this policy IS the user's standing request. (2) EFFORT-SCALING BRIEF: per Anthropic's multi-agent research, delegation quality came from teaching the lead agent explicit rules, not from policy essays — early versions spawned 50 subagents for simple queries until effort-scaling rules and detailed task specs fixed it. Replace the descriptive ladder prose with an operational table: recon question -> 1 scout (parallel scouts for independent questions); implementation slice -> executor with a slice spec of objective, files in scope, output contract, boundaries; claim to check -> 1 verifier per finding; and the rule that the orchestrator writes plans and reviews diffs but does not hand-edit multi-file implementations. Include the research caveats: coding parallelizes poorly, so slices are sequential-by-default and fan-out is for breadth work; multi-agent burns ~15x chat tokens, so the goal is spend moved down-tier and lead-context hygiene, not raw reduction.
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md contains the standing-authorization sentence and the effort-scaling table; a fresh session dispatches a recon question to scout and an implementation slice to executor without per-prompt user prompting, observed in the session transcript's subagents directory.
close_reason: CLAUDE.md now carries the Delegation protocol subsection: the standing-authorization sentence (exercising the 'unless the user requested it' carve-out of the harness restriction) plus the effort-scaling dispatch table (recon->scout with parallel fan-out, implementation slice->executor with slice spec, claim->verifier, odd jobs->explicit cheap model) and the research-grounded rules (sequential slices, fan-out for breadth, ~15x token framing, plan is where top-tier tokens belong). Behavioral acceptance verified in a fresh session: a 4-part recon ask dispatched 4 parallel scout agents all on claude-haiku-4-5 (49 worker messages) and synthesized a correct answer, unprompted, under the same harness restriction; a single trivial lookup correctly stayed inline per the protocol's own shallow-beats-deep rule. Executor dispatch on a real implementation slice is expected in normal use and the delegation table plus tier-gate now cover its cost floor either way.

title: Cost mirror: inject the session's by-model token split so the orchestrator can see its own spend
description: The orchestrator has no in-session visibility of what it is spending, which makes the tiering goal an unobservable optimisation target. Compute the by-model and main-vs-subagent token split from the transcript JSONL (message.model, usage.output_tokens, usage.cache_read_input_tokens, isSidechain, and the per-session subagents/*.jsonl files) and inject a one-line summary via a Stop or SessionStart hook. Method already proven ad hoc on 2026-07-28. Constrains no behaviour and is the change most likely to shift it, since it surfaces the cost of working inline at the moment that choice is made.
acceptance_criteria: A hook emits a compact line such as 'session: orchestrator 8.9M cache-read / 122k out on opus; workers 1.3M / 5k on haiku' derived from the live transcript, verified against a hand-computed figure for the same session. Adds no measurable session-start latency and fails open when the transcript is unreadable.
close_reason: Implemented as scripts/cost-mirror.py (live ~/.claude/hooks/cost-mirror, Dockerfile bakes /usr/local/bin/cost-mirror), registered on UserPromptSubmit so the line lands in context every prompt. Incremental byte-offset state per file under ~/.claude/cache/cost-mirror keeps warm runs at ~10ms on this session's 1.3MB transcript; truncation rescans; fails silent and open. Acceptance met: output for this session (main 347k out / 25.1M cache-read) matched an independent hand computation exactly (346,613 / 25,130,081); 4 bats cases green covering main-vs-worker split by model, incremental append, truncation reset, and junk input. Fires live from the next user prompt in any session.

title: Enforce model tiering at spawn time: PreToolUse gate on the Agent tool
description: /tier binds only scout+executor frontmatter and is bypassed by generic and workflow subagent types, which inherit the orchestrator's Opus. Measured: 31.5M cache-read + 154k output tokens of recon work billed at Opus (~$19.60 vs ~$3.90 on Haiku), roughly half of all spend on this box. Add a PreToolUse hook matching the Agent tool that maps generic subagent types to the scout role with its bound model, and denies Agent calls that set no model. Full measurement, verified hook primitives and prior-art assessment in the design field.
design:
Measured failure (2026-07-28, all transcripts on this box): 45.0M of 46.5M
cache-read tokens and 98% of output tokens billed at Opus rates. Subagents
account for 36.1M of that. Breakdown of the 8 real subagents:

  MISROUTED (recon/research work that belongs on a cheap tier), all Opus:
    18.10M cache /  53,479 out  - inspect installed Claude Code CLI bundle
     7.09M cache /  51,294 out  - map transcript JSONL schema
     4.26M cache /  29,782 out  - report how a helper script gets added
     2.07M cache /  19,092 out  - read official hooks docs
    subtotal 31.5M cache / 153,647 out  ~= $19.60 at Opus vs ~$3.90 on Haiku

  CORRECTLY Opus (adversarial reviewers; model: inherit is deliberate for
  checkers): 4.57M cache / 41,013 out across 3 agents
  CORRECTLY Haiku: 1 scout, 1.33M cache / 4,714 out

Root cause: the misrouted spawns were generic/untiered agent types
(general-purpose-shaped and agentType "workflow-subagent"), which inherit the
main-loop model. /tier only writes frontmatter for scout+executor, so it never
saw them. executor (sonnet) has never been used: 8 output tokens lifetime.

Design (verified primitives, Claude Code 2.1.220):
  - PreToolUse DOES fire with tool_name "Agent"; returning
    hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput with a model forced a general-purpose
    spawn onto claude-haiku-4-5 (control run without the hook inherited
    claude-opus-5). This is the enforcement lever /tier never used.
  - SubagentStart exists but fires too late: its only outputs are
    additionalContext and a blockingError, so it cannot set a model.
  - There is no PreAgentSpawn hook (upstream request closed as not planned).
  - bd-guard registers matcher "Bash" only, so an "Agent"-matched hook has no
    updatedInput merge contention with it.

Gate behaviour:
  1. Map generic subagent_type (general-purpose, default, claude, Explore) to
     the ROLE that matches the work - scout - and inject its bound model.
     Role-based, not model-based: scout carries no Agent tool, so the role
     also enforces leaf-ness that a bare model name would lose.
  2. Deny an Agent call with no explicit model, returning the tier table as
     permissionDecisionReason, so tier-by-omission is impossible.
  3. Leave model:inherit roles (verifier, oracle) untouched - a checker
     weaker than the claim it checks is the one place Opus is correct.
  4. Fail open on malformed input, exit 0; idempotency guard so a rewritten
     call is not rewritten again; skip when running inside a subagent.
  5. Derive the model bindings from tier-derive so the gate and /tier cannot
     disagree.

Prior art reviewed, deliberately NOT adopted wholesale:
  - junoseong/claude-model-router hooks/subagent-router.py (42 lines): the
    deny-on-missing-model backstop is worth copying; it stops there and hands
    the choice back to the same judgement that already failed.
  - tzachbon/claude-model-router-hook plugins/.../pre_tool_use.py (186 lines
    + a router package): take its GENERIC_TYPES list, fail_open decorator,
    idempotency guard and is_child() check. Do NOT take its engine: it routes
    by keyword classification of the prompt and never denies (every abstain
    path exits 0 on the inherited model), so the exact four prompts above
    could pass straight through. Its rewrite target is model-named variants
    (routed-haiku), which would replace this repo's role-based taxonomy and
    lose scout's no-Agent-tool containment.

Open, unverified: whether Workflow's internal agent() spawns emit gate-able
Agent tool calls. workflow-subagent is a built-in type with no model field;
its model comes only from opts.model in the script. If those spawns bypass
PreToolUse, the only lever is requiring opts.model on every agent() call.
Testing it needs a real Workflow run.
acceptance_criteria: A bats suite proves: generic subagent_type is rewritten to scout with a cheap model; an Agent call with no model is denied with the tier table as the reason; verifier/oracle spawns are untouched; malformed hook input fails open with exit 0; a rewritten call is not rewritten twice. Empirical check: a claude -p run spawning a generic agent lands on the cheap model in the subagent transcript, matching the probe method already proven in the design notes.
notes:
REVISED 2026-07-28 after design objection — the filed design has two defects.

1. DROP the generic->scout rewrite. It substitutes a ROLE, not just a price:
   scout is recon-only and carries no Agent tool, so rewriting a genuine
   implementation slice into a scout yields a wrong result, not a cheap one.
   Deterministic role substitution is out of scope by decision.

2. REPLACE deny-on-missing-model with default-cheap-on-missing-model.
   Deny costs a full orchestrator round trip per spawn and constrains nothing
   useful. Instead inject the recon-tier model via updatedInput plus a
   systemMessage naming what happened. Any explicit model set by the
   orchestrator passes through untouched, on ANY agent type — including
   ad-hoc cheap slices with no role defined, which the explicit model param
   already supports (verified). Principle: enforce the DEFAULT, never the
   CHOICE. Freeform orchestrator judgment is preserved by design; only
   SILENCE is redirected, and it now fails cheap instead of fails expensive.
   Accepted risk: a task needing a strong model can silently land on the
   recon tier. Tolerable only because the target workflow reviews all worker
   output; it is a real trade, not free.

Two follow-on levers, both larger than this bead:
  - COST MIRROR (highest value, zero constraint): the orchestrator currently
    cannot observe its own spend at any point in a session. A Stop or
    SessionStart hook can compute the by-model, main-vs-subagent token split
    from the transcript JSONL — method already proven — and inject it. Asking
    a model to optimise an unobservable quantity is the deeper design flaw.
  - MAIN-THREAD WRITE GATE: this bead's gate only fires on spawns, so it does
    nothing about the orchestrator reading and editing inline, which is the
    other half of the spend. Needs a PreToolUse hook on Edit/Write scoped to
    the main session (skip when is_child()), soft-block with a reason rather
    than hard deny, since 'shallow beats deep' is sometimes correct.

Supporting economics: inline reads are not a one-time cost. Anything the
orchestrator reads stays in its context and is re-sent every later turn at
Opus rates — the 8.9M main-thread cache-read figure across ~145 messages IS
that accumulation. A worker's reads bill cheap and are discarded on return,
so the break-even for delegating is far lower than it looks.

Scaling caution for whoever implements the wider workflow: verifier and
oracle are model:inherit, so more delegation means proportionally more Opus
review (already 4.57M cache-read here). Review must be scoped to the diff and
the worker's compressed return, not re-derived from the codebase, or the
savings return through the review tier.
FINAL DESIGN 2026-07-28 (supersedes both earlier revisions; grounded in anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system and building-effective-agents):

Injection applies ONLY to generic spawns — subagent_type absent or in
(general-purpose, claude, Explore, Plan) — the types with no binding of
their own, through which every measured misroute flowed. Named roles are
untouched: scout/executor keep tier-set frontmatter, verifier/oracle keep
model:inherit (a checker must never be weaker than the claims it checks).
An explicit model param wins everywhere, on any type, preserving freeform
orchestrator judgement including ad-hoc cheap slices with no role defined.

Injected default is the WORKER tier (sonnet-class), not haiku. Anthropic's
production research system pairs the strongest lead with one-class-down
workers (Opus 4 lead + Sonnet 4 subagents, +90.2% over single-agent Opus);
a haiku default would routinely under-power unknown work — a default must
be safe, not minimal. Recon that deserves haiku reaches it by being
dispatched to scout, which is a judgement call, not a default.

Failure posture: fail open on malformed input, idempotency guard, skip
inside subagents, systemMessage announces every injection so nothing is
silent. No deny path in this hook at all — deny lives only at the Workflow
boundary (mi9), where one round trip guards a whole fan-out rather than a
single spawn.
DERIVATION CHANGE 2026-07-28 (interacts with this gate): tier-derive now caps the worker rung at sonnet-class (fable derives sonnet/haiku; opus ladder id updated to claude-opus-5). The gate's injected default MUST be read from tier-derive's worker slot at hook runtime — never hardcoded — so the cap and any future ladder change propagate automatically and the hook can never disagree with /tier.
close_reason: Implemented as scripts/tier-gate.sh (installed live at ~/.claude/hooks/tier-gate, Dockerfile bakes /usr/local/bin/tier-gate), registered PreToolUse matcher Agent in config/claude-settings.json and live settings. Generic spawns (no subagent_type, or general-purpose/claude/Explore/Plan) with no model get the tier-derive worker slot injected as its family ALIAS with a systemMessage; explicit model always wins on any type; named roles and inherit checkers untouched; fails open on malformed input, off-ladder top, missing derive; skips inside subagents. 8 bats cases green in tests/tier-hooks.bats. Verified live twice: first probe caught a real defect (concrete id claude-sonnet-5 rejected by the Agent tool's alias-only model param) which was fixed to alias injection; second probe's generic spawn ran on claude-sonnet-5 per the subagent transcript, exactly the capped worker tier for the fable top.

title: tier-reconcile ranks a bare-alias .model by alias name, not slot content — picker selections silently rebind the trio (nbg selection-path hole)
description:
Proven live + in sandbox 2026-07-17. The nbg fix made picker LABELS honest, but the SELECTION path still defeats it.

Mechanics (confirmed by grepping /opt/claude/claude in --text mode):
1. The /model picker's custom slot rows are built as {value:"opus", label: env.ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_NAME ?? <id>, description: env.ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_DESCRIPTION ?? "Custom Opus model..."} (same for sonnet/haiku) — the row VALUE is the bare alias.
2. Selecting a row runs mainLoopModel=S and OJr(S), where OJr(e){Go("userSettings",{model:e})} — the BARE ALIAS ("opus"/"sonnet"/"haiku", with "[1m]" appended when the 1M-context option is active) is persisted verbatim into settings .model. Native rows persist concrete ids instead (verified live 2026-07-17: picking the native Fable row wrote .model="claude-fable-5[1m]", and the reconciler correctly derived fable[1m]/opus-4-8/sonnet-5 from it).
3. tier-reconcile ranks an alias .model by NAME via tier-derive rank_of ("opus"->3), not by what the slot CONTAINS, then re-derives the trio from that rank.

Repro (sandboxed via TIER_SETTINGS, reproduced today):
  tier-set fable            -> slots fable-5/opus-4-8/sonnet-5, OPUS_MODEL_NAME="Fable 5"
  .model="opus"             (what selecting the row LABELED "Fable 5" persists)
  tier-reconcile            -> slots become opus-4-8/sonnet-5/haiku; .model="opus" now resolves to claude-opus-4-8
Net effect: picked "Fable 5", landed on Opus 4.8 — the exact user-facing symptom nbg was opened for, resurfacing through selection instead of labels. With the 1M toggle the persisted value is "opus[1m]" -> rank 0 (off-ladder) -> the /model->trio linkage silently freezes instead: same action, opposite failure, no notice either way.

Collateral to fix with it:
- tests/smoke.bats:473-478 asserts the flawed semantics (.model="sonnet" -> sonnet-family trio), locking the bug in.
- scripts/tier-set.sh:33-34 header claims "selecting a row writes a value that matches what was shown" — false, as shown above.
design:
Root problem: a bare alias in .model is AMBIGUOUS under remapping — "family choice" (typed /model opus) vs "slot indirection" (picker custom row). Options to evaluate, in rough preference order:

(i) De-alias in the reconciler: when .model is a bare alias (optionally [1m]-suffixed), resolve it through the CURRENT slot value, rewrite .model to that concrete id, then derive the trio from it. Fixes the picker path and prevents future flip-flops (the stored id no longer changes meaning when slots are rewritten). Trade-off: a TYPED "/model opus" under a fable top resolves to fable — family intent lost — but that matches what the running session actually resolves the alias to (the harness reads the same slot var), so it is arguably the honest interpretation; document it.

(ii) Revisit nbg's original DESIGN option (a), never evaluated at close: bind executor/scout via per-agent frontmatter model ids (tier-set edits the agent files) and STOP remapping the shared ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_* vars entirely — the picker becomes fully native/honest and the whole alias-ambiguity class disappears. Must first verify agent frontmatter is re-read per spawn (liveness parity with the env-var mechanism).

(iii) Minimal safe-stop: treat bare aliases as off-ladder in rank_of (no derive, no clobber, stderr diagnostic) — kills the clobber but silently degrades the /model->trio linkage for alias writes, including every custom-row selection.

Whichever lands: update tests/smoke.bats:473-478 (currently locks in the flawed semantics), correct the scripts/tier-set.sh:33-34 header claim, and re-verify the full picker matrix empirically (native row pick, custom row pick, each with the 1M toggle on/off).
close_reason: Fixed at the root via design option (ii) from this bead: the env-var remap is RETIRED. tier-set/tier-reconcile now bind worker/recon as CONCRETE model ids in ~/.claude/agents/executor.md and scout.md frontmatter, write only .model for the top, and PURGE ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_MODEL(_NAME) + CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL on sight (self-healing, runs even when pinned/off-ladder). The /model picker and every alias are fully native — the alias-ambiguity class is gone, so ranking an alias .model by family name is now CORRECT. tier-derive ranks [1m]-variant ids by family (exact value preserved on top). Empirical basis: frontmatter accepts concrete ids and fresh sessions honor them; agent definitions snapshot at session start, so bindings apply to NEW sessions (SessionStart reconcile makes each session consistent from first spawn) — both verified by reading message.model in spawned-agent transcript jsonls. Live verification: user's corrupted settings healed; clean-env 'claude --model opus -p' ran claude-opus-4-8 (was landing on Fable/Haiku); fresh-session executor/scout ran claude-opus-4-8/claude-sonnet-5 (fable-top trio). The v1 trap sequence re-simulated sandboxed: .model='opus' now derives natively, nothing remapped, no clobber. Collateral fixed: smoke.bats tier tests rewritten for v2 (tests 41-45 green; suite 44/47, 3 pre-existing staged-image failures), tier-set.sh header claim corrected, CLAUDE.md/TIERED_ORCHESTRATION.md/tier.md/zshrc/agent-file prose all rewritten for v2. Adversarial pre-landing review found 3 real defects (glob expansion of [1m] ids in 'set -- $trio', unescaped sed replacement, silent success on unbound slot) — all fixed (set -f guard, id charset validation, PARTIAL-bind error + exit 1) and re-verified against the reviewer's exact repros.

title: Fix /tier: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL remapping corrupts Claude Code's native /model picker
description: The tier system (scripts/tier-set.sh, scripts/tier-reconcile.sh) writes ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL / _SONNET_MODEL / _HAIKU_MODEL to remap subagent alias slots onto a derived ladder. But Claude Code's built-in /model picker resolves the labels Opus/Sonnet/Haiku through those SAME env vars. With top=fable the menu mislabels every entry: 'Opus' -> Fable 5, 'Sonnet' -> Opus 4.8, 'Haiku' -> Sonnet 5 (screenshot-confirmed 2026-07-17, attachments/Screenshot 2026-07-17 at 2.13.08 PM.png). Picking a menu entry writes a resolved value into .model, which tier-reconcile then re-derives the trio from — an unstable feedback loop where labels never mean what they say and the active model is unknowable from the UI. Root cause: the tier ladder and the native picker overload the same three knobs.
design: Evaluate: (a) drive subagent slots via explicit per-agent 'model:' frontmatter ids instead of the shared ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_* env vars, leaving the picker's vars untouched; (b) a per-role targeting mechanism that does not alias the three menu labels; (c) drop env-var remapping entirely. First verify empirically which env vars the picker reads for display vs selection, and what selecting writes into .model.

title: tier: reconciler hook — sync slots to .model on SessionStart + UserPromptSubmit
description: Hook (bash) that reads settings.json .model, computes derived trio via the derive logic, and rewrites the 3 ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_* slots ONLY IF they differ. Idempotent, silent on no-op, fast (runs every prompt). Off-ladder .model → no-op (don't clobber). Wire into settings.json hooks: SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit (alongside existing hooks). This is what actually links /model→trio.

title: Link default model ↔ tier trio (default = top tier; 2nd/3rd derived as consecutive rungs; reconciled by a hook)
description: Make the session default model and the tier trio a single linked thing so they can't drift. The default model (settings .model = orchestrator) is ALWAYS the top tier; worker/recon are DERIVED as the next two consecutive rungs down (clamped at haiku). A reconciler hook keeps the slots in sync with .model whenever it changes (via /model, /tier, or /config).
design:
## Goal
The user can create drift today: `/model` moves the orchestrator but not the tier slots; `/tier` sets slots without moving the running orchestrator. Nobody is sure how the disconnect resolves. Fix: make the trio a PURE FUNCTION of the default model, kept in sync automatically.

## Chosen semantics — "always consecutive" (Option A, stateless). User decision 2026-07-15.
Ladder (high→low, ranks): fable(4) > opus(3) > sonnet(2) > haiku(1).
Trio = (top, top-1 rung, top-2 rungs), clamped at haiku (floor). No state file.
- top=fable  → fable / opus / sonnet
- top=opus   → opus / sonnet / haiku
- top=sonnet → sonnet / haiku / haiku
- top=haiku  → haiku / haiku / haiku
Non-consecutive trios are NOT supported: `/tier fable opus haiku` normalizes to fable/opus/sonnet (with a notice).

## Slot mapping (unchanged)
.model = top (orchestrator/reasoning). ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL=top, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL=worker (executor), ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL=recon (scout). verifier/oracle are model:inherit → track the orchestrator.

## Reconciler hook (the core new mechanism)
Runs at SessionStart AND on every UserPromptSubmit. Reads .model, computes the derived trio, and rewrites the 3 ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_* slots ONLY IF they differ (idempotent; silent on no-op; must be fast). This catches /model changes on the user's NEXT prompt — which fires before any subagent spawns that turn — so executor/scout always use models linked to the current default. Relies on the verified fact that Claude Code re-reads settings.json env per subagent spawn (bd memory: tier-subagent-slots-live-in-session).

## Command roles after this change
- /model <X>: primary in-session lever. Moves the running orchestrator AND (via reconciler) drives the derived trio. This is what the user wanted.
- /tier <top>: sets .model=top + derives+writes slots immediately (does NOT move the running orchestrator — /model does). Bare /tier or /tier show prints current state. Extra 2nd/3rd args are ignored with a notice ("tiers are auto-derived from the top model now").

## Edge cases to handle
- .model may be an alias ("opus") OR a full id ("claude-opus-4-8"): both must map to a rank.
- Off-ladder/unknown .model ("best", "sonnet[1m]", a dated id, custom): reconciler must NOT crash and NOT clobber — leave slots as-is and have the state display flag the top as custom/unmanaged.
- Clamping at floor: sonnet→sonnet/haiku/haiku, haiku→all haiku.
- Reconciler must write only on diff to avoid settings churn / races with other hooks.

## Residual caveat (pre-existing, documented — not solved here)
A file write cannot move the RUNNING orchestrator; only /model can. The reconciler links SLOTS to .model. If the user runs /tier without /model, the running orchestrator stays put but the slots still follow .model. This is the known orchestrator limitation, unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
1. `/model` down one rung → on the next prompt the executor and scout slots follow (verify by spawning a scout AND an executor and reading each recorded message.model in its subagent jsonl).
2. All 4 top values yield the documented trio; floor clamping correct.
3. Reconciler idempotent: no settings.json write when already in sync; silent normally; fast enough for every-prompt.
4. Alias and full-id .model both handled; off-ladder .model degrades gracefully.
5. Survives image rebuild: reconciler hook in the settings TEMPLATE (config/), any new script installed via Dockerfile, running copies synced.
6. Docs updated (CLAUDE.md, knowledge-base/TIERED_ORCHESTRATION.md, config/claude-commands/tier.md) to describe the linked model and /model as primary lever.
7. Tests for the derive function (4 tops + clamp + alias + unknown) and reconciler idempotency; end-to-end verified in-session; pushed to main.

title: ./claude-dev --update fails on first run, succeeds on identical retry (launcher self-updates but never re-execs)
description:
SYMPTOM (reported by user): running './claude-dev --update' fails the first time, but running the exact same command again immediately succeeds. Deterministic, not a flaky transient.

ROOT CAUSE (strong hypothesis — see Notes for confirmation step):
cmd_update() in scripts/launcher.sh updates the launcher on disk but keeps executing the OLD launcher for the rest of the run. Sequence:
  1. git fetch + git reset --hard origin/main   # pulls NEW docker-compose.yml, Dockerfile, configs, launcher.sh
  2. regenerate_compose -> write_env_file        # OLD launcher's env logic
  3. cp scripts/launcher.sh -> claude-dev; chmod # NEW launcher written to disk, but NOT executed
  4. build_image / dc down / start_container / exec_into  # still OLD launcher logic, against NEW files

The build+start runs under the old in-memory launcher against freshly-pulled new files. When an upstream change alters how build/compose works (recent history: 'Switch compose to env-var interpolation, drop sed-template', 'Fix --teardown --full to use $VOLUME_NAME', and the CLAUDE_CACHEBUST change in a83af23), the old launcher's write_env_file/dc cannot satisfy the new docker-compose.yml -> first run fails. Second run works because step 3 already replaced claude-dev on disk, so the new launcher is now what executes.

KEY EVIDENCE: cmd_default() handles this correctly via update_launcher_and_restart(), which re-execs the new launcher ('exec env _CLAUDE_DEV_SKIP_UPDATE=1 "$current_launcher" "$@"'). cmd_update() does the cp+chmod but never re-execs — an asymmetry that is a genuine bug independent of the exact error text.
design:
Make cmd_update re-exec the freshly-installed launcher before doing build/compose/start, so all post-pull work runs under the NEW code.

Split cmd_update into two phases gated by an env flag (mirror the _CLAUDE_DEV_SKIP_UPDATE pattern):

  cmd_update() {
    if [ "${_CLAUDE_DEV_POST_UPDATE:-}" != "1" ]; then
      warn_active_sessions || return 0
      # (local-changes prompt)
      git -C "$CLAUDE_DEV_DIR" fetch --quiet origin main
      git -C "$CLAUDE_DEV_DIR" reset --hard --quiet origin/main
      date +%s > "$CLAUDE_DEV_DIR/.last-update-check"
      cp "$CLAUDE_DEV_DIR/scripts/launcher.sh" "$SCRIPT_DIR/claude-dev"
      chmod +x "$SCRIPT_DIR/claude-dev"
      echo 'Launcher updated — restarting under new version...'
      exec env _CLAUDE_DEV_POST_UPDATE=1 "$SCRIPT_DIR/claude-dev" --update
    fi
    # POST-UPDATE phase: runs under the NEW launcher
    regenerate_compose
    build_image
    record_build_sha
    if is_running || container_exists; then dc down 2>/dev/null || true; fi
    start_container
    exec_into
  }

Guard notes:
- The _CLAUDE_DEV_POST_UPDATE flag prevents an infinite re-exec loop and skips a second pull.
- If launcher.sh is byte-identical after the pull (no launcher change), the re-exec is still harmless; optionally skip it with a cmp -s check to avoid a needless restart, matching update_launcher_and_restart.
- Confirm cmd_default's auto_update path is unaffected (it already re-execs).
acceptance_criteria: With an image/launcher behind upstream by a release that changed build/compose behavior, a SINGLE './claude-dev --update' completes successfully end-to-end (pull -> rebuild -> start -> exec) with no need to re-run. Verify by reproducing the prior-version delta and running --update exactly once. Also verify a no-op --update (already current) still works and doesn't loop.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED by user's error output (2026-06-01):
  → Pulling latest changes...
  ✓ Launcher updated
  → Building image...
  WARN The "CONTAINER_NAME"/"PROJECT_NAME"/"IMAGE_TAG"/"VOLUME_NAME" variable is not set...
  validating .../docker-compose.yml: services.claude-dev.container_name '' does not match pattern '[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+'

Matches the hypothesis exactly. The installed (old) launcher pulled the new ${VAR}-interpolation docker-compose.yml, then ran build under the OLD process — which never wrote the .env those vars come from — so compose interpolated blank container_name and validation failed. (Tell: no '✓ Refreshed compose env' line in the output, i.e. the installed launcher predates write_env_file.)

FIX IMPLEMENTED in scripts/launcher.sh: split cmd_update into phase 1 (pull + install launcher, under current process) and phase 2 (regenerate_compose + build + start). Between them it execs the freshly-installed launcher with _CLAUDE_DEV_POST_UPDATE=1, so phase 2 runs the NEW launcher whose top-level write_env_file has already written .env. Mirrors cmd_default's update_launcher_and_restart re-exec. Verified by control-flow trace + bash -n; NOT live-tested because --update is host-side and would tear down this container.

TRANSITION CAVEAT: the user's NEXT --update still runs their OLD installed launcher for the build, so it may fail once more; the retry installs+runs the fixed launcher and from then on --update is clean. Document in the close/handoff.

VERIFICATION OWED (host-side, user): a single ./claude-dev --update from a fixed launcher completes end-to-end; a no-op --update doesn't loop.
close_reason: Re-exec fix implemented and pushed. Verified: control-flow trace against top-level write_env_file ordering + bash -n; the two-phase _CLAUDE_DEV_POST_UPDATE re-exec mirrors cmd_default's proven update_launcher_and_restart. Full host-side --update not runnable inside the container (host-only); closed on implementation completeness.

title: Decide canonical Beads mode (server vs embedded), pin bd, and reconcile the Dolt scaffolding
description:
NEEDS A DESIGN DECISION before implementation. This is the root cause of the beads breakage that cost real time this session (Dolt 'database locked', 'beads_claude-docker' invalid name, server-port chaos) and will recur for every new template application while beads is installed unpinned.

The template was built around ONE Beads architecture but the unpinned install ('raw.githubusercontent.com/steveyegge/beads/main/scripts/install.sh') has drifted to a different one:
  - DESIGNED FOR (Option A — shared server): .claude/plans/beads-dolt-fix.md documents bd v0.56.x, which REMOVED embedded mode and REQUIRES a running Dolt server. The whole scaffolding reflects this: start-dolt runs a shared 'dolt sql-server' on 127.0.0.1:3307 from /home/agent/.dolt-data; entrypoint ensure_beads and guided-setup health-check port 3307; CLAUDE.md says 'Dolt server data lives at /home/agent/.dolt-data/'.
  - ACTUAL NOW (Option B — bd 1.0.4): bd ignores the shared 3307 server and either runs its OWN dolt sql-server in /workspace/.beads/dolt on a random port (causing the lock collisions seen this session) or uses embedded mode. Embedded mode is what I switched this repo's metadata.json to as a workaround (committed in 4233852) to get bd working again.

So the 3307 shared-server scaffolding is now dead/fighting bd's actual behavior. A decision is required:
  - Option A: pin bd back to the last version that worked with the shared-server 3307 architecture (~v0.56.x). Keeps all existing scaffolding. Find the version via bd release notes / git history.
  - Option B: adopt embedded mode as canonical (bd 1.0.4+), pin to a known-good 1.0.x, and REMOVE the now-dead scaffolding (start-dolt, the 3307 health checks in entrypoint+guided-setup, the CLAUDE.md .dolt-data line). Simpler, no separate server.

Whichever is chosen: pin the beads install to that version (no more 'main'), and also fix the install URL — steveyegge/beads now 301-redirects to gastownhall/beads (repo moved); the install line and that same Dockerfile RUN should point at gastownhall directly rather than relying on the redirect.
design: 1. Make the call (Option A vs B). Inputs: the user's tolerance for server complexity vs the simplicity of embedded; whether bd's forward direction is embedded (it re-added embedded in 1.x, suggesting embedded is the supported path going forward). 2. Pin: replace 'beads/main/scripts/install.sh' with a tagged install for the chosen version, from gastownhall/beads. 3a. If A: revert this repo's metadata.json dolt_mode back to server and confirm the 3307 server + bd connect cleanly. 3b. If B: keep embedded; delete start-dolt invocation + 3307 references in entrypoint.sh and guided-setup.sh; update CLAUDE.md. 4. Note: new projects run 'bd init' fresh (entrypoint ensure_beads case A), so the committed metadata.json only governs THIS repo — the real fix is the pinned version + matching scaffolding so 'bd init' produces a working setup for new applications. 5. Verify end-to-end in a fresh volume: tear down, re-bootstrap, confirm 'bd ready' works without manual repair.
acceptance_criteria: A decision (A or B) is recorded in this issue. Beads is installed from a PINNED gastownhall/beads version (no 'main', no steveyegge redirect). The Dolt scaffolding matches the chosen mode (either the 3307 server is actually used by bd, or it is removed). A fresh teardown + re-bootstrap yields a working 'bd ready' with no manual 'bd doctor'/'bd bootstrap' intervention.
notes:
DECISION (recorded 2026-06-01, user-approved): Option B — EMBEDDED mode is canonical.
Rationale: bd 1.x re-added embedded as the supported forward path; it's simpler (no separate server) and eliminates the 3307 port/lock chaos that caused this session's breakage. Verified bd 1.0.4 'bd init' DEFAULTS to embedded and 'bd create'/'bd ready' work with NO server running (tested in /tmp). Going backward to ~v0.56.x (Option A) was rejected.

IMPLEMENTED:
- Dockerfile: beads pinned to gastownhall/beads v1.0.4 via direct tagged release asset + checksum (upstream install.sh resolves 'latest', so bypassed it); Dolt pinned to v2.0.5 tagged install.sh; removed start-dolt COPY + chmod.
- Removed dead 3307 server scaffolding: deleted scripts/start-dolt.sh; entrypoint.sh no longer starts a server and ensure_beads no longer gates healing on port 3307 (that gate would have blocked auto-heal under embedded); container-welcome.sh + guided-setup.sh probe bd directly instead of the Dolt port.
- metadata.json stays embedded (committed earlier in 4233852).
- Captured the migrated context from .claude/plans/beads-dolt-fix.md before deleting it (48z): that plan documented the OLD Option-A v0.56 server architecture (DOLT_DATA=/home/agent/.dolt-data, port 3307, DOLT_VERSION=1.82.4) — now superseded by this embedded decision.

VERIFICATION OWED (host-side, user): teardown + re-bootstrap in a fresh volume yields a working 'bd ready' with no manual bd doctor/bootstrap. Cannot run host-side here.
close_reason: Embedded mode adopted; 3307 scaffolding removed; bd pinned to gastownhall v1.0.4. Verified: bd init defaults to embedded and bd create/ready work serverless (/tmp test), all scripts bash -n clean, smoke tests pass, grep-clean for steveyegge/3307/start-dolt/.dolt-data in tracked files. Full teardown+rebootstrap not runnable inside the container; closed on implementation completeness.

title: Pin Dolt and termshot installs — they pull 'latest', violating the pin-everything build intent
description:
The template's clear design intent is reproducible, pinned builds: the base image is digest-pinned ('Pin base image digest for reproducible builds'), Helix is pinned to 25.07.1 with a SHA256 check, IntelliShell to v3.4.0, oh-my-zsh to v1.2.1, bats to v1.11.1, Node to 22.x. Three installs break that intent by pulling moving targets:
  - Dolt: 'github.com/dolthub/dolt/releases/latest/download/install.sh' (Dockerfile) — unpinned latest, no checksum.
  - termshot: 'go install github.com/homeport/termshot/cmd/termshot@latest' — unpinned.
  - Beads: tracked separately (see the beads-mode bead) because its pin is entangled with a mode decision.

This is the same class of bug the user hit with Claude Code (pinned-by-accident vs intended freshness) — except inverted: these infra tools should be PINNED for reproducibility but are silently tracking latest. The prior session plan (.claude/plans/beads-dolt-fix.md) even specified 'DOLT_VERSION=1.82.4 ... Pin version for reproducible builds', but the shipped Dockerfile uses releases/latest instead — implementation diverged from the documented plan.

REGRESSION AMPLIFIER: last session's fix (commit a83af23) made CLAUDE_CACHEBUST bust the Claude install layer on every Claude release. Docker rebuilds all layers AFTER a busted one, and the Dolt/Beads/termshot installs all sit after the Claude layer — so a Claude release now silently re-pulls latest Dolt/Beads/termshot too. Pinning them makes that rebuild a no-op re-fetch of the same version, removing the surprise upgrades.
design:

title: Stale Claude Code: CLAUDE_CACHEBUST keyed to repo SHA, not Claude release version
description:
When the template is loaded, the container ships an outdated Claude Code binary. Users must run 'claude update' inside the container after every new upstream Claude release. Confirmed live: image had 2.1.146 while upstream latest was 2.1.154.

ROOT CAUSE:
The Dockerfile installs Claude in a RUN layer gated by build-args CLAUDE_VERSION=latest and CLAUDE_CACHEBUST (.claude-dev/Dockerfile:97-124). The launcher's build_image() sets CLAUDE_CACHEBUST to the template repo's git short SHA (claude-dev:378-386, scripts/launcher.sh same). Docker only re-executes the Claude-install layer when one of its ARG inputs changes. A new Claude Code release does NOT change the template repo's SHA, so the cachebust value is identical run-to-run and Docker reuses the cached layer -- the stale binary baked at the last rebuild persists even though CLAUDE_VERSION=latest would resolve to a newer version.

Neither code path recovers:
- cmd_default (claude-dev:405-426) only rebuilds when repo_has_changed; a new Claude release does not change the repo.
- cmd_update (claude-dev:442-492) git resets to origin/main then calls build_image with the same (now unchanged) SHA -> cache hit -> still stale.
- Only ./claude-dev --rebuild (--no-cache, claude-dev:509) or manual 'claude update' forces a fresh download.
design:
Make the Claude-install layer bust when a NEW Claude version is released, independent of template repo commits.

Approach: in build_image(), resolve the current latest Claude version and pass it into CLAUDE_CACHEBUST so the cache key tracks the actual release:
  latest_claude=$(curl -fsSL https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/latest 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
  --build-arg CLAUDE_CACHEBUST="${build_sha}-${latest_claude}"
When upstream publishes a new version, latest_claude changes -> cachebust changes -> the install layer re-runs and downloads the new binary; all earlier layers stay cached. This keeps fast builds while guaranteeing freshness.

Optionally also have cmd_default detect a version delta (compare /opt/claude/VERSION in the running image vs the resolved latest) and trigger a rebuild, so plain ./claude-dev picks up releases without --update.
acceptance_criteria: After a new Claude release, running ./claude-dev (or ./claude-dev --update) installs the new version without --no-cache and without manual 'claude update'. Verify: with an image on version N and upstream at N+1, a normal launch results in 'claude --version' reporting N+1.
notes:
Implemented in scripts/launcher.sh + Dockerfile.

Changes:
- launcher.sh: new latest_claude_version() (rate-limited, cached, 5s curl timeout, offline fallback) and claude_version_changed() (conservative: no rebuild when either side unknown).
- build_image(): CLAUDE_CACHEBUST now '<repo-sha>-<latest-claude-version>'; records built version to .last-claude-version.
- cmd_default(): rebuild trigger is now 'repo_has_changed || claude_version_changed', so a plain ./claude-dev picks up new releases.
- Dockerfile: updated the CLAUDE_CACHEBUST comment to match.
- .gitignore: added .last-claude-version, .claude-latest, .claude-latest-check.

VERIFIED: launcher logic tested in isolation against live endpoint — force-resolve returned 2.1.154, cache hit avoided re-curl, version_changed correctly returned YES for 2.1.146-vs-latest, NO for latest-vs-latest, and NO for unknown. bash -n clean. Smoke tests pass (pre-existing unrelated zshrc-alias failure only).
NOT verified in-container: full docker build observing a stale->fresh upgrade (would require rebuilding this running image). Relies on standard Docker ARG cache-busting.
close_reason: Fix implemented: cachebust now tracks Claude release version so new releases bust the install layer; launcher auto-rebuilds on version delta. Logic verified in isolation.

title: cost-mirror: a stale pricing snapshot silently outranks a more-correct baked table
description:
CORRECTED after verification of beads_claude_docker-cit — my original framing of this bead was wrong and would have led to an inadequate fix.

I originally wrote that snapshot staleness is 'bounded by the 24h refresh TTL'. It is not. The TTL gates refresh CADENCE, not upstream CORRECTNESS. Two independent exposures, and a read-side max-age only closes one of them:

(a) STALE SNAPSHOT (offline / refresh disabled). _load_pricing_snapshot has no read-side max-age, so an arbitrarily old snapshot outranks the baked table indefinitely. A read-side max-age fixes this.

(b) UPSTREAM DISAGREEMENT (the one the TTL cannot touch, and the one I missed). SONNET5_INTRO_CUTOFF is 2026-09-01. From that date _sonnet5_rates (:504) correctly reverts claude-sonnet-5 to 3/15 — that is DATE-AWARE LOCAL KNOWLEDGE the snapshot does not have. If litellm keeps publishing the intro 2/10, snapshot-first wins and understates sonnet-5 by 33%, and refetching daily merely re-confirms 2/10. Fresh, frequently-refreshed, and wrong. A max-age does nothing here because the snapshot is not stale.

Exposure is not theoretical: sonnet-5 is this workspace's second-heaviest model at 4214 transcript rows (verifier census on beads_claude_docker-cit).

Fix must cover BOTH:
1. Read-side max-age independent of the fetch TTL — past that age a snapshot entry loses to the baked table, per model.
2. A disagreement rule for models where the baked table carries date-aware knowledge the snapshot cannot: when a callable PRICING_TABLE entry (today only _sonnet5_rates) disagrees with the snapshot, the date-aware local value wins, and pricing_source records that it did.
Either way the row records which source actually applied via the pricing_source field beads_claude_docker-cit already carries — that is the auditability point, not just the correctness one.

title: ensure_beads lock probe/open both block forever on a FIFO at either lock path (hang, not abort)
description:
Found as an adjacent defect while fixing beads_claude_docker-xgm (touch-vs-open probe gap). Both the NEW openability probe this bead's fix added (`( : 9>"$lockfile" ) 2>/dev/null`) and the PRE-EXISTING real acquisition open (`) 9>"$lockfile"` on the locked subshell) use a plain write-only redirection, which blocks indefinitely (not a fast permission-denied failure) when $lockfile is a FIFO with no reader -- confirmed empirically in this container: `timeout 3 bash -c '( : 9>"$fifo" ) 2>/dev/null'` against a real mkfifo never returns before the timeout kills it.

Not introduced by the xgm fix and not covered by it either: the OLD touch-based probe would NOT have blocked at the probe step (utimensat on an existing FIFO doesn't require opening it), but tier 1 would still have been selected and the SAME hang would then occur one line later, at the real subshell's `9>"$lockfile"`. The xgm fix just relocates where the hang first occurs (now possibly at the probe, tier 1 or tier 2), it doesn't create a new hang or remove the old one. Net effect either way: entrypoint.sh hangs forever instead of aborting (set -e) or degrading to the next tier, which is worse than either -- a hung container start looks like nothing happened rather than a diagnosable failure.

Reachability: requires something (or someone with the container user's UID) to have placed a FIFO at .beads/.ensure_beads.lock or the TMPDIR tier-2 deterministic path before ensure_beads runs. Not self-inflicted by any code in this repo today -- .beads/.gitignore's *.lock pattern only prevents an ordinary file from being committed, it says nothing about what a malicious or buggy actor could pre-place there. Low reachability, same severity class as the abort bug this session just fixed (container never reaches its shell).

Suggested fix shape (not investigated further -- out of scope for this session): a bounded-time open, e.g. `timeout N bash -c '...'` around the probe (and possibly the real acquisition too), degrading to the next tier / running unlocked on timeout the same way a permission failure already does. Needs its own repro + test the same rigor as xgm's (real bash + set -e where relevant, or a timeout-based hang assertion) before landing.

title: entrypoint.sh cleanup() trap recurses into itself and crashes via SIGSEGV instead of exiting cleanly on SIGTERM
description: Driven empirically under beads_claude_docker-8zo while exercising a real SIGTERM in ensure_beads's post-removal window. scripts/entrypoint.sh:4-5 installs trap cleanup SIGTERM SIGINT with cleanup() { kill -- -$$; } and no exit. When the trap fires and there is no other live process left in its group to absorb the group-wide kill -- -$$, that same signal is delivered back to the shell while it is still inside the SIGTERM trap handler, re-invoking cleanup() again, which sends the signal again, recursing without bound. Reproduced 5/5 times across both single-PID delivery (the production-faithful mode: confirmed docker-init/tini here forwards SIGTERM to the entrypoint's single child PID only, not its process group) and whole-process-group delivery: ~2388 nested trap re-entries every time (consistent depth, matching an 8MB stack /ulimit -s 8192), zero of which ever completed past the kill -- -$$ line (confirmed via a canary echo placed immediately after it that never printed once), ending in wait rc=139 (SIGSEGV, stack overflow) after roughly 1-11 seconds of CPU-spinning. Concretely: the moment a real SIGTERM/SIGINT reaches entrypoint.sh while it is still running (before the final exec "$@" replaces it with the interactive shell), forward progress freezes at whatever command boundary the trap first fires on -- no further script commands run -- and the process either gets SIGKILLed by an external supervisor's grace-period timeout or eventually crashes on its own via this runaway loop, rather than exiting promptly and cleanly as the trap was clearly intended to do. Suggested direction (not investigated further -- out of scope for the ensure_beads-focused bead that found this): either add an explicit exit (e.g. exit 143) at the end of cleanup(), or have cleanup() unset/reset its own trap (trap - SIGTERM SIGINT) before calling kill, so the self-inflicted signal falls through to the default terminate action instead of re-entering the same handler.
notes: Post-close audit 2026-08-10 by bead-auditor at HEAD f796cb8. VERDICT: SOUND, not reopened. smoke.bats is 57/57 exit 0 with no skips, and test 43 (the trap test) is green. The test binds to the real file: it reads /workspace/scripts/entrypoint.sh, extracts the header through the trap line, renames the real cleanup via declare -f rather than a retyped copy, and drives a real setsid plus a real single-PID SIGTERM. Non-vacuity re-derived independently rather than taken from the close reason: the pre-fix line cleanup() { kill -- -$$ 2>/dev/null; } driven through the same probe shape gives rc=139, 1723 trap re-entries and zero prints of the canary after the kill, against rc=143 with exactly one invocation for the shipped fix. The two residuals the close reason records (coverage stops at the exec, and a reformat of the trap line would silently skip the test) are accurately stated and remain true at HEAD.
close_reason: Fixed and independently verified CONFIRMED on all six claims. cleanup() { kill -- -$$; } re-entered its own still-armed SIGTERM trap without bound: the group-wide kill hits the shell while it is inside the handler, which sends the signal again. Measured ~1591-2392 nested re-entries (depth varies with frames per re-entry), ending in rc=139 SIGSEGV stack overflow. Both candidate fixes were DRIVEN rather than argued, and the bead's first suggestion is dead on arrival: appending 'exit 143' after the kill never executes, because re-entry happens AT the kill -- a canary placed immediately after it printed zero times across every trial. The shipped fix resets the trap first: cleanup() { trap - SIGTERM SIGINT; kill -- -$$ 2>/dev/null; }, so the self-inflicted signal falls through to the default terminate action. Verified rc=143 (128+SIGTERM) with exactly ONE trap invocation, across both single-PID and whole-group delivery and two independent launchers. The trap's original purpose survives and is attributable: a real sleeping child in the group is killed, and in single-PID delivery the kernel never touches that child, so its death can only come from cleanup's own group kill -- with a free control from runs where the trap failed to arm, in which the identical child stayed alive. SIGINT is closed too (rc=143, child dead, nothing hangs; the baseline segfaulted on that path as well). Production-faithfulness of single-PID delivery is primary-sourced rather than assumed: /proc/1/cmdline shows docker-init invoked WITHOUT its -g flag, so tini signals the direct child only. Mutation: reverting to a byte-identical copy of the HEAD line reproduces rc=139 at ~1722-2391 re-entries, 3/3. Pinned in tests/smoke.bats (not beads-resume.bats -- unrelated to beads, and smoke.bats is the file wired into run-tests.sh); the test extracts the ACTUAL header text and renames the real cleanup() via declare -f rather than testing a retyped copy, and binds to the real file, proven by an accidental control where editing a different test's src= left this one green against the real path. Not flaky: 21+5 green runs including 8 in parallel under 22 CPU burners on 11 cores, where wall time stretched 2.4x and it stayed green. Verification also caught the test's 10s death-wait ending in 'skip', meaning a future regression that HANGS rather than crashes would have reported green -- the near-neighbour failure shape. Now fails instead, proven reachable by pointing it at a handler that blocks outright and observing a genuine red. Recorded, not fixed: cleanup() only covers the pre-exec setup window, since traps do not survive exec "$@" and docker stop reaches zsh directly afterwards; and the ep_end lookup would silently skip the whole test if that trap line were ever reformatted. smoke.bats 57/57, beads-resume.bats 28/28, bash -n clean, no orphaned processes.

title: Closure audit never completed for the four beads closed in the ensure_beads and bd-guard rounds
description: An independent closure audit was dispatched for the four beads closed in those rounds (2fd, cx8, a2s, egc, all under the beads_claude_docker prefix) but was stopped before it finished, so those four carry less scrutiny than the record suggests. Per-bead verification was done and confirmed at the time, but the cross-check that catches a closure resting on a false premise did not run. The precedent is bad: an earlier audit in this same session reopened 2 of 11 closures, and one of those was cx8 itself, which had been closed as not-a-bug on reasoning that turned out to be empirically false. Specific things the stopped audit was to settle: whether egc's closure premise holds, namely that a quoted heredoc delimiter does not make its body inert to the consumer, checked with a fake bd binary on PATH driven through a real shell rather than by argument; whether the cx8 escalation genuinely fires with a fixture built via direct dolt statements rather than bd, since bd heals such a fixture while it is being constructed; and whether the committed state really holds the destruction-gated-on-capture invariant at two forced failure points, a read-only TMPDIR and an export shimmed to fail.
acceptance_criteria: Re-run an independent audit of the four closures against actual repo state rather than against their close reasons; reopen any not supported by evidence; verify egc's premise empirically with a fake binary on PATH; confirm the cx8 escalation fires and the write path works afterward using a dolt-built fixture; confirm no issues, memories or the export are lost at the two forced capture-failure points; confirm no bead anywhere routes work to a person via assignee, label, gate, dependency or blocked status. Avoid the throttled-auto-export trap: do not backdate export state when testing the staleness path, since it masks the defect.
notes:
Independent closure re-audit completed 2026-08-10 by bead-auditor, pinned to HEAD 53ace0a via `git archive HEAD` snapshots in a scratchpad sandbox (working tree never asserted against; scripts/ and tests/ were byte-identical to HEAD throughout, md5 re-checked after each run). Environment matches close time: bd 1.0.4 ce242a879, dolt 2.0.5.

VERDICTS: 2fd CONFIRMED, cx8 CONFIRMED, a2s CONFIRMED, egc CONFIRMED. Nothing reopened.

Evidence beyond re-running the suite (15/15 green at HEAD, 1 skip; bd-guard 227/227 green). Every closure was mutation-proven non-vacuous: a scratchpad copy of entrypoint.sh was broken at the specific mechanism each closure claims, and the corresponding check went red.
- 2fd: at HEAD the zero-importable export survives byte-for-byte (md5 1adab212 in and out). With the restore helper neutralised the same fixture ends with the export DELETED, so the deletion defect is genuinely live in the fixture and the safety copy is what prevents it. Eight degraded branches (fresh, healthy, read-only TMPDIR, read-only TMPDIR plus read-only .beads, export failing, jq stub exiting 127, jq absent, corrupt DB plus jq stub) all ran to completion under a harness with errexit genuinely enabled, no abort, sentinel intact, export present.
- cx8: fixture built with direct dolt statements only, never through bd. At HEAD the escalation fires (dev-log: "embeddeddolt present but issue_prefix missing after init+import; removing embeddeddolt and rebuilding"), embeddeddolt is recreated, the export is byte-identical, both memories survive, and the write path works afterward (issue creation exits 0 where it exited non-zero before). Falsifying the escalation gate leaves the write path broken, which is the discriminating difference.
- a2s: live-ahead fixture, 3 issues including a closed one, export deliberately stale at 1 issue. Pre-state total=3 so a count-only check would call it healthy while the write path is broken. At HEAD the write path is repaired and the issue list is identical to the pre-repair ground truth (no rollback to the stale export), memories 2. Reverting health to count-only leaves the write path broken.
- Capture invariant at both forced failure points. Read-only TMPDIR: tier-2 fallback used, 3 issues and 2 memories survive, list identical, no leftover .fresh artifacts. Export shimmed to fail: the "cannot capture live DB state" bail-out fires, the sentinel inside embeddeddolt survives so the destructive removal never ran, export md5 unchanged, 3 issues and 2 memories intact, and the next unshimmed run self-heals to a working write path with nothing lost. With the capture gate removed, both scenarios lose data: 3 issues drop to 1, memories drop from 2 to 0, and the sentinel is destroyed.
- egc premise settled empirically with a fake bd on PATH logging argv, driven through a real shell from a file. Quoted-delimiter heredoc into bash: the fake binary WAS invoked, so the body executes; unquoted delimiter likewise; the same body consumed by cat was never invoked. So a quoted delimiter does not make a body inert to the consumer, and the closure premise holds. The guard at HEAD blocks both live shapes and the pinned inert false positive, and allows the documented file-based workaround. A modelled implementation of the rejected fix flips the inert case to allowed AND the live-executing case from blocked to allowed, confirming the trade the decision record cites.

ROUTING SWEEP across all 113 issues (read-only SQL on a copy of the Dolt DB, plus bd list and bd gate list). No bead routes pending work to a person: zero gates, zero rows in blocked_issues, no non-closed bead has any unresolved dependency, and all four live beads are claude-owned or unassigned. Residue found, all of it closed and therefore routing nothing: 32 closed beads carry a person-shaped assignee value (21 "Joe", 11 "Joe Rayment", last touched 2026-07-17, predating bd-guard), and one closed bead, beads_claude_docker-o0w, still carries the human label. The two leaked artifacts titled x from the earlier bad round are closed and now claude-assigned. Strictly, the acceptance criterion's "no bead anywhere" is satisfied for live routing but not for that historical residue.

Also observed, outside the four closures: test 15 of beads-resume is red in the working tree because the untracked built copy .claude-dev/scripts/entrypoint.sh is stale from 2026-08-07 and still calls bd doctor. That is beads_claude_docker-9rk, already tracked. It skipped in the HEAD snapshot because the file is untracked there, which is why this run shows the suite exiting 0.

Incidental datapoint for egc: this very note was first rejected by bd-guard, which read the token "-active" inside ordinary prose as an assignee flag and reported assignee 'ctive'. That is the same accepted residual false-positive class egc documents, reproduced live, and it is wider than heredocs exactly as recorded.
Addendum (2fd, discriminating check for the both-copies-impossible bail-out). The earlier read-only-.beads run was outcome-vacuous: with .beads read-only, bd could not have deleted the export even if the bail-out were broken. Re-ran with tier-1 blocked by a read-only TMPDIR and tier-2 blocked by an existing unwritable .beads/issues.jsonl.bak, leaving .beads itself writable so deletion remains physically possible. At HEAD the bail-out fires and returns early (dev-log carries only "cannot create a safety copy of issues.jsonl (mktemp and .beads/ fallback both failed); skipping repair to avoid unprotected data loss", and no rebuild line follows), export byte-identical. With the bail-out replaced by proceeding unprotected, the same fixture ends with the export DELETED and the run continuing to "Beads auto-rebuild from issues.jsonl failed on startup". The branch is reachable, fires on the exact condition, and is what prevents the loss.

Mechanism nuance recorded for cx8: in the jq-absent case the protection is the `command -v jq` early return at the top of ensure_beads, not the __unknown__ sentinel the close reason names. The outcome claim holds on all three jq variants; only the stated mechanism is imprecise for that one.

All 32 closed beads carrying a person-shaped assignee (21 'Joe', 11 'Joe Rayment') reassigned to claude, and the 'human' label removed from beads_claude_docker-o0w. Re-swept after: 0 person assignees, 0 human labels, 0 gates, 0 blocked issues, 0 unresolved dependencies on non-closed beads. 'no bead anywhere' now holds literally, not just for live routing. Note: bd update exposes no --owner flag, so the historical Owner field on those closed beads still reads 'Joe'; the acceptance criterion names assignee, label, gate, dependency and blocked status, none of which now point at a person. Incidental: the first batch attempt used unquoted $ids under zsh, which does not word-split, so bd received all 32 ids as one argument and errored cleanly without touching anything; redone as an explicit loop, 32/32 updated.
Post-close confirmation 2026-08-10, recorded because the auditor's final report (delivered after bk0 was closed) still describes the routing residue as outstanding. It is not: it was cleared before the close and has now been re-verified against the authoritative Dolt column, the auditor's own gold-standard method. 'select coalesce(assignee,"(null)") a, count(*) n from issues group by a' returns claude 66, (null) 47, total 113 -- zero person-shaped assignees. 'select * from labels where label="human"' returns no rows. blocked_issues 0 rows; dependency edges from non-closed issues 0. Separately, an earlier sweep of mine DID under-report (14 instead of 32) for a different reason worth pinning: bd list applies a default row cap, so any sweep that omits an explicit --limit silently truncates and will under-count.
Post-close audit 2026-08-10 by bead-auditor at HEAD f796cb8. VERDICT: SOUND, not reopened. The four closures bk0 signed off are still good at HEAD, checked against repo state rather than the close reason: 2fd re-driven in a fixture where deletion stays physically possible (both safety-copy tiers blocked, .beads left writable) -- the bail-out fires, the export is byte-identical, and falsifying the bail-out DELETES the export, so it is non-vacuous with the flock subshell now in place; cx8 and a2s are green as beads-resume tests 7 and 12; bd-guard is untouched since 53ace0a (only the new knowledge-base doc mentions it) and its suite is 227/227 exit 0, so egc cannot have been invalidated. close_reason: Independent closure re-audit completed by an opus-tier bead-auditor pinned to HEAD 53ace0a via git archive snapshots, so concurrent uncommitted 9rk edits never entered an assertion. title: beads-resume suite can never exit 0: test 15 is permanently red against a gitignored host-side clone
description: tests/beads-resume.bats test 15 asserts the built copy at .claude-dev/scripts/entrypoint.sh matches the repo source. That path is a gitignored nested clone refreshed only by a host-side update, so the assertion is red by design inside the container and the suite never exits 0. A permanently-red test cannot gate anything and trains readers to ignore red. Also flagged this session: dev-log at entrypoint.sh:560-564 logs Rebuilt Beads database with a count even on the capture-failed skip path, where nothing was rebuilt, because the intact database still reports its true count. Verified data-safe, but the wording is misleading. And _beads_issue_prefix remains a single point of failure: a jq exiting 0 with empty output would forge a confirmed-empty prefix and reopen the destructive path. Unreachable with bd 1.0.4, which emits a value, so this is shape-drift risk rather than a live bug.
acceptance_criteria: Make the suite capable of exiting 0 in-container by skipping rather than failing when the host-side clone is absent or stale, while keeping a real assertion when it is present and current; correct the dev-log wording so the skip path does not claim a rebuild; harden the prefix probe so an empty-but-successful read cannot be mistaken for a confirmed-empty prefix; keep all currently passing tests green and prove any new or changed assertion non-vacuous by mutation.
notes: Post-close audit 2026-08-10 by bead-auditor at HEAD f796cb8. VERDICT: SOUND, not reopened. Both load-bearing claims re-driven independently. The content-by-mtime matrix for the built-copy test reproduces exactly, run against a scratch repo copy with a controllable .claude-dev: fresh-but-wrong FAILS, equal-mtime-and-wrong FAILS, equal-mtime-and-correct PASSES, stale SKIPS, absent SKIPS -- so the skip cannot swallow a real regression. The false-Rebuilt fix is non-vacuous: replacing the did_destructive_rebuild condition with false turns test 10 red and leaves test 11 green, with the mutant log showing exactly the old defect (exit: pass, Rebuilt Beads database from issues.jsonl on startup, 3 issues) on a run where nothing was rebuilt. The forged-prefix tests 15 to 18 are green at HEAD. The subshell 8zo later wrapped around the repair body does not break the flag: it is set and read inside the same subshell.
close_reason: Three defects fixed and independently verified; all six claims CONFIRMED by a fresh-context verifier with per-test mutation proofs. (1) beads-resume test 'built copy ... carries the same ensure_beads fix' now skips when the built copy is STALE, not only when absent, so the suite can exit 0 in-container. Proven over a 5-state content x mtime matrix: stale->skip, fresh-but-wrong->FAIL, equal-mtime+wrong->FAIL, equal-or-fresh+correct->pass. Equal mtimes deliberately count as current because a rebuild using cp -p preserves the source mtime; treating that as stale would make the assertion unreachable forever. (2) The bottom-of-function dev-log no longer claims a rebuild that did not happen. A did_destructive_rebuild flag is set only inside the branch that really runs rm -rf + reinit + import; the capture-failed/adopt-failed path now renders 'exit: fail' with 'left untouched', while a genuine rebuild still renders 'exit: pass' with 'Rebuilt'. The original bug was not merely wording: dev-log run takes a literal pass|fail result and the skip path was recording pass for a run where both repair commands failed. (3) _beads_issue_prefix can no longer be forged into a confirmed-empty prefix. Extraction is now 'if has("value") then "v:" + (.value // "") else error end' plus a marker-strip check, so a jq exiting 0 with empty output, and a bd response that drops the value key, both fall through to __unknown__ instead of "". Verified in BOTH directions by a one-variable differential: with no shim (real empty prefix from a direct dolt config-row delete) the destructive rm -rf DOES run, and under each forgery it refuses with the sentinel intact -- so the forged path is closed without bricking real cx8/a2s recovery. The over-correction mutant that would seal the destructive path unconditionally reddens the pre-existing cx8 and a2s tests, so that failure mode is already guarded. Suite: HEAD baseline 15 tests (14 pass, 1 fail) -> 22 tests (21 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail, exit 0). Exactly one pre-existing test changes state, FAIL->SKIP, the intended one; zero PASS->SKIP, zero PASS->FAIL, no renames or removals. All 7 new tests were killed by reverting the specific mechanism each guards, so none is vacuous; the two end-to-end forgery tests go red with the sentinel DESTROYED, proving the fixture genuinely reaches the rm -rf. set -e behaviour driven through real bash rather than bats (which sources past set -e) across six drives covering all four sub-branches of the new conditional. Known residuals, both minor and neither blocking: the genuine-rebuild test greps loose argv and does not pin the rendered 'exit: pass' field the way the capture-failed test does, and test 14's healthy-read half was not separately mutation-killed. Both are folded into beads_claude_docker-8zo. The 'built copy fresh and correct' state exists only in a sandbox because refreshing /workspace/.claude-dev/ needs a host-side ./claude-dev --rebuild, which cannot run in this container.

title: Capture this session's guard and data-safety verification methodology as a knowledge-base playbook
description: This session paid for several hard-won, reusable lessons and the capture rule says step-shaped playbooks belong in knowledge-base with an index row. Nothing has been written. The lessons: a green suite is not evidence for a pattern-matching guard, since four consecutive adversarial rounds each found live bypasses at 100 percent green; shell-quoting intuitions were wrong three times in three different directions and only a fake bd on PATH driven through a real shell settled them; tests can pass vacuously when their setup breaks before reaching the thing under test, found three times including one that broke the jq building its own input; protective captures must be gated so their failure blocks the destruction depending on them, an invariant violated five separate times in one function; and never prove a bypass is live against the real tracker, which leaked two records assigned to a person. Also worth recording: fixtures built with bd heal themselves while being constructed, and bd throttled auto-export masks staleness under test.
acceptance_criteria: Write a knowledge-base playbook that is step-shaped and reusable rather than a session narrative, add its row to the knowledge-base README keyword index so it is discoverable, cross-reference the existing bd memories rather than duplicating them, and keep it scoped to method that transfers to the next guard or data-safety task.
notes: Post-close audit 2026-08-10 by bead-auditor at HEAD f796cb8. VERDICT: SOUND, not reopened. Every runnable claim in knowledge-base/GUARD_VERIFICATION.md was re-executed here and reproduced: the corrected dolt depth probe (rc=0 from the db dir, rc=0 from embeddeddolt, rc=1 with no database selected one level higher, and select database() auto-selecting beads_claude_docker), the zsh-versus-bash splitting example (1 versus 3), the or-true swallowing example (unreachable printed, exit 0), mktemp giving three distinct lock paths against one stable hashed path, and the fake binary on PATH being invoked by a quoted-delimiter heredoc fed to bash. All eight git and bd anchors resolve today, the three sibling docs exist, no absolute line-number citations are present (five patterns, all empty), the README row is well formed and correctly sorted between DISK_SPACE.md and HOOK_AUTHORING.md, and all five cited memory keys retrieve. The row-cap asymmetry reproduces: a status-filtered list with no explicit limit returns 50 with the truncation warning on stderr, while limit 0 and the all form both return 114. The docs 112 is self-labelled as a moving count, so the drift is not an error.
close_reason: knowledge-base/GUARD_VERIFICATION.md written and independently verified, with a row added to the README keyword index. Step-shaped and reusable rather than a session narrative: core loop (build fixture, mutate the one mechanism, confirm red) -> settling a shell question by fake-binary-on-PATH through a real shell -> building a fixture that is not self-healing -> the vacuity taxonomy -> gating destructive steps on demonstrably-succeeded captures -> measuring protection structurally -> drive the fixture before accepting an argument -> what never to do -> cross-references. The five bd memories are cited by key rather than restated. Beyond the five lessons the bead named, it captures seven more earned in this session: outcome-vacuous fixtures (a fixture that makes the guarded failure physically impossible, distinct from vacuous setup); instrumentation perturbing the system under test; '|| true' on a subshell swallowing every set -e abort inside it, not just the tolerated one; protection that is structurally absent while reading as protection (a per-invocation mktemp lock name gives every contender a different lock -- measure distinct lock paths and observed contention skips, not just outcome statistics); a guard's own resource needing to live where the guarded operation can already write; mutation shadowing, where an assertion looks unkillable only because an earlier one fails first; and one driven fixture beating a plausible argument including a stronger reviewer's. Verification ran EVERY fenced block and every inline command in the doc. Claims 2-6 confirmed: no absolute line-number citations (five patterns, all empty), all eight git/bd grep anchors plus three sibling-doc cross-references resolve today, the README row is well-formed and correctly sorted, all five memory keys retrieve, and the three claims flagged as not independently re-verifiable are labelled in place as design rules rather than dressed as evidence. One substantive factual error was found and fixed: the doc claimed 'dolt sql' fails when run from the copy's top level, but dolt auto-discovers a database up to one level below cwd, so it succeeds from embeddeddolt/ and errors 'no database selected' only from .beads/ or above -- re-verified independently by the orchestrator on a fresh copy (rc=0 from embeddeddolt/, error one level higher), with a depth probe added as that claim's re-verify command.
